title: Medical ethics, law and professionalism
audience: a medical student in the preclinical years
purpose: Apply the principles of medical ethics to consent, capacity and surrogates, confidentiality, minors, reproduction, the end of life, errors and disclosure, conflicts of interest, justice and access, research ethics and the law clinicians must know.
primary_reading: University of Washington: Ethics in Medicine

weeks.10: Justice, equity and access to care
weeks.12: Law for clinicians: malpractice, reporting and duties

blocks.deliverable: Analyze a consent case with the four principles.
Explain when confidentiality may be broken.
Explain consent rules for minors and their exceptions.
Week 7 midterm; plan an error disclosure conversation.
Analyze a case of resource allocation.
Explain mandatory reporting duties and the elements of negligence.
Submit the project; take an unseen 150 minute final in week 14.

project: Ethics consultation: analyze three supplied cases with a structured method and write a recommendation that addresses the counterarguments.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
